rules.title: High percentage of clients connecting without PQC support
rules.desc: Identifies PQC Proxy instances where more than 50% of TLS handshakes in the last 24 hours used classical (non-PQC) key exchange because clients did not offer any post-quantum groups. This is an adoption tracking signal - these clients are not protected against harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks. Consider requiring client TLS library upgrades or communicating PQC requirements to connecting services.
rules.query:
PQCProxy_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventType == "handshake"
| summarize Total = count(), Classical = countif(QuantumPosture == "classical") by ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId
| where Classical * 100.0 / Total > 50
| extend ClassicalPct = round(100.0 * Classical / Total, 1)
| project ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId, Total, Classical, ClassicalPct
| order by ClassicalPct desc

rules.title: PQC downgrade detected - client offered hybrid but classical was negotiated
rules.desc: Identifies TLS handshakes where the client offered a post-quantum hybrid key exchange group (X25519MLKEM768 or X25519Kyber768Draft00) but the negotiation fell back to a classical group (X25519 or P-256). This may indicate a misconfigured PQC Proxy, a middlebox stripping PQC groups from ClientHello, or an active downgrade attack. Investigate the proxy configuration and network path between client and proxy.
rules.query:
PQCProxy_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType == "downgrade"
| project TimeGenerated, ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId, ClientIP, NegotiatedGroup, OfferedGroups, CipherSuite, Metadata
| order by TimeGenerated desc

rules.title: PQC Proxy certificate expiring within 7 days - immediate renewal required
rules.desc: Identifies PQC Proxy instances serving a TLS certificate that expires within the next 7 days. Immediate certificate renewal is required to prevent service outage. Clients will receive TLS errors once the certificate expires, breaking all PQC-protected connections through the proxy.
rules.query:
PQCProxy_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventType == "cert_expiry"
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by ProxyInstanceId, CertPath
| where CertExpiryDays <= 7
| project TimeGenerated, ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId, CertPath, CertExpiryDays, Metadata
| order by CertExpiryDays asc

rules.title: PQC Proxy certificate expiring within 30 days
rules.desc: Identifies PQC Proxy instances serving a TLS certificate that expires within the next 30 days. Certificate renewal should be performed before expiry to avoid service disruption. If the certificate is renewed, ensure the replacement uses a PQ-hybrid or classical algorithm compatible with TLS 1.3 and the configured key exchange groups.
rules.query:
PQCProxy_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventType == "cert_expiry"
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by ProxyInstanceId, CertPath
| where CertExpiryDays <= 30
| project TimeGenerated, ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId, CertPath, CertExpiryDays, Metadata
| order by CertExpiryDays asc

rules.title: TLS handshake failure spike on PQC Proxy
rules.desc: Identifies an elevated rate of TLS handshake failures on a PQC Proxy instance within the last hour. This may indicate clients using incompatible TLS libraries, expired or invalid certificates, a denial-of-service attempt, or network-level interference with the TLS handshake. Investigate the error messages and client IPs to determine the root cause.
rules.query:
PQCProxy_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType == "tls_error"
| summarize ErrorCount = count(), DistinctClients = dcount(ClientIP), Errors = make_set(ErrorMessage, 5) by ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId
| where ErrorCount > 10
| project ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId, ErrorCount, DistinctClients, Errors
| order by ErrorCount desc

rules.title: Upstream backend connection failures on PQC Proxy
rules.desc: Identifies PQC Proxy instances experiencing elevated upstream connection failures when forwarding requests to backend services. This may indicate the backend is down, overloaded, or unreachable. While the PQC Proxy TLS termination is functioning correctly, clients will receive 502/504 errors until the backend recovers.
rules.query:
PQCProxy_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType == "upstream_error"
| summarize ErrorCount = count(), Errors = make_set(ErrorMessage, 5) by ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId, UpstreamTarget
| where ErrorCount > 5
| project ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId, UpstreamTarget, ErrorCount, Errors
| order by ErrorCount desc

fp: Deployments, build steps, application jobs, and administrative scripts may run shells from a web application directory. Review the command argument, parent PID, service ownership, and nearby HTTP traffic. Hex-encoded EX…

Forward /var/log/audit/audit.log with the Splunk Universal Forwarder and install Splunk Add-…

`linux_auditd`
(
    (
        type=SYSCALL
        key="process_creation"
        success="yes"
        exe IN (
            "*/ash",
            "*/bash",
            "*/busybox",
            "*/csh",
            "*/dash",
            "*/fish",
            "*/ion",
            "*/ksh",
            "*/mksh",
            "*/sh",
            "*/tcsh",
            "*/zsh"
        )
    )
    OR
    (
        type=EXECVE
        a0 IN (
            "ash", "*/ash",
            "bash", "*/bash",
            "csh", "*/csh",
            "dash", "*/dash",
            "fish", "*/fish",
            "ion", "*/ion",
            "ksh", "*/ksh",
            "mksh", "*/mksh",
            "sh", "*/sh",
            "tcsh", "*/tcsh",
            "zsh", "*/zsh",
            "busybox", "*/busybox"
        )
    )
    OR
    (
        type=CWD
        cwd IN (
            "/app",
            "/app/*",
            "/dev/shm",
            "/dev/shm/*",
            "/home/*/*",
            "/home/*/*/*",
            "/opt/*",
            "/srv/http",
            "/srv/http/*",
            "/srv/www",
            "/srv/www/*",
            "/usr/share/nginx/html",
            "/usr/share/nginx/html/*",
            "/var/lib/tomcat*/webapps",
            "/var/lib/tomcat*/webapps/*",
            "/var/www",
            "/var/www/*"
        )
    )
)

| rex field=msg "audit\\((?<audit_event_id>[^)]+)\\)"

| eval shell_exec=if(
    type="SYSCALL"
    AND key="process_creation"

        lower(exe),
        "(^|/)(ash|bash|busybox|csh|dash|fish|ion|ksh|mksh|sh|tcsh|zsh)$"

rules.title: Classical fallback - PQC VPN tunnel established without quantum protection
rules.desc: A WireGuard tunnel was established using classical X25519 key exchange because the remote peer does not support ML-KEM-768 hybrid key exchange. The PQC policy was set to "prefer" or "allow", so the connection was permitted but is NOT protected against harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks. All traffic through this tunnel can be recorded and decrypted by a future quantum computer. Upgrade the remote peer to support PQC VPN Overlay.
rules.query:
PQCVPNOverlay_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType_s == "classical_fallback"
| project TimeGenerated, PeerID_s, PeerAddress_s, KeyExchange_s, PolicyMode_s, HNDLRisk_d, Metadata_s
| order by TimeGenerated desc

rules.title: High harvest-now-decrypt-later risk rate across VPN tunnels
rules.desc: More than 30% of active PQC VPN tunnels in the last 24 hours were established without quantum protection (HNDLRisk_d=1). Traffic through these tunnels is vulnerable to harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks. This is an adoption tracking signal -- review which peers lack PQC support and prioritize their upgrade to ML-KEM-768 hybrid key exchange.
rules.query:
PQCVPNOverlay_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventType_s == "tunnel_up"
| summarize Total = count(), AtRisk = countif(HNDLRisk_d == 1) by bin(TimeGenerated, 1d)
| extend HNDLPct = round(100.0 * AtRisk / Total, 1)
| where HNDLPct > 30
| project TimeGenerated, Total, AtRisk, HNDLPct

rules.title: New peer connected without PQC - quantum protection not available
rules.desc: A previously unseen peer was discovered and connected to the PQC VPN Overlay without post-quantum key exchange. This peer is using classical WireGuard only and traffic is vulnerable to harvest-now-decrypt-later. New peers should be provisioned with ML-KEM-768 hybrid key exchange support from the start to ensure quantum-safe connectivity.
rules.query:
let knownPeers = PQCVPNOverlay_CL
| where TimeGenerated between (ago(2d) .. ago(1d))
| distinct PeerID_s;
PQCVPNOverlay_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventType_s == "peer_discovered"
| where PQCUsed_d == 0
| where PeerID_s !in (knownPeers)
| project TimeGenerated, PeerID_s, PeerAddress_s, KeyExchange_s, PolicyMode_s, HNDLRisk_d

rules.title: Excessive tunnel rekeying on PQC VPN Overlay
rules.desc: An abnormally high number of session rekey events was detected for a peer within a short period. While periodic rekeying is expected (every ~120 seconds by default), a spike may indicate network instability, peer crashes and reconnects, or an attempt to exhaust KEM resources through repeated handshakes. Investigate the peer and network path.
rules.query:
PQCVPNOverlay_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType_s == "tunnel_rekey"
| summarize RekeyCount = count() by PeerID_s, PeerAddress_s
| where RekeyCount > 20
| project PeerID_s, PeerAddress_s, RekeyCount
| order by RekeyCount desc

rules.title: PQC VPN tunnel handshake failure
rules.desc: A hybrid post-quantum WireGuard handshake failed. This may indicate key material incompatibility between peers, ML-KEM key encapsulation failure, network-level interference with the Noise IK handshake, or a peer running an incompatible PQC VPN Overlay version. Investigate the error message and peer address. Repeated failures from the same peer may indicate an attack or misconfiguration.
rules.query:
PQCVPNOverlay_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType_s == "handshake_fail"
| project TimeGenerated, PeerID_s, PeerAddress_s, KeyExchange_s, PolicyMode_s, ErrorMessage_s, Metadata_s
| order by TimeGenerated desc

rules.title: PQC VPN policy blocked a connection
rules.desc: The PQC VPN Overlay policy engine blocked a peer connection. This occurs when PQCPolicy is set to "require" and a peer does not support hybrid post-quantum key exchange. The peer attempted to establish a classical WireGuard tunnel but was rejected because the policy mandates PQC protection. Either upgrade the remote peer to support ML-KEM-768 or change the policy to "prefer" to allow classical fallback.
rules.query:
PQCVPNOverlay_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType_s == "policy_block"
| project TimeGenerated, PeerID_s, PeerAddress_s, KeyExchange_s, PolicyMode_s, PolicyAction_s, ErrorMessage_s
| order by TimeGenerated desc

rules.title: Linux Auditd Service Crash and Restart Burst
rules.desc: This analytic detects repeated Linux process crash events followed by repeated successful executions of the same executable on the same host within 10 seconds. A rapid crash and restart pattern in a service process can indicate exploitation attempts or unstable application behavior and should be correlated with network and application telemetry.
rules.author: Raven Tait, Splunk
fp: Application defects, resource pressure, and supervisor restart policies can produce repeated crashes and restarts. Review the affected executable, user, parent process, host role, and related application or network acti…
rules.how: To implement this detection, the process begins by ingesting auditd data, that consists of SYSCALL, TYPE, EXECVE and PROCTITLE events, which captures command-line executions and process details on Unix/Linux systems. These logs should be ingested and processed using Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux…
rules.query:
`linux_auditd`
(
    type=ANOM_ABEND
    OR
    (
        type=SYSCALL success="yes"
        (
            syscall IN ("59", "221", "11")
            OR
            SYSCALL="execve"
        )
    )
)

| eval exe=coalesce(exe, executable), event_type=if(type="ANOM_ABEND", "crash", "start")
| eval sig=coalesce(sig, signal)

| where event_type="start" OR tonumber(sig) IN (6, 7, 11)

| sort 0 _time

| streamstats time_window=10s count(eval(event_type="crash")) as crash_count max(eval(if(event_type="crash", _time, null()))) as last_crash_time values(eval(if(event_type="crash", sig, null()))) as crash_signals by host exe

| eval restart_after_crash=if(event_type="start" AND _time>last_crash_time, 1, 0)

| streamstats time_window=10s sum(restart_after_crash) as restart_count by host exe

| where event_type="start" AND crash_count>=2 AND restart_count>=2

| stats min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime max(crash_count) as crash_count max(restart_count) as restart_count values(crash_signals) as crash_signals values(comm) as process_name values(uid) as uid values(auid) as auid values(ppid) as parent_pid by host exe

| rename host as dest

| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| `linux_auditd_service_crash_and_restart_burst_filter`

This activity is significant as adversaries commonly use various encoding schemes to obfuscat…

rules.query:
`zeek_http`
method="POST"
post_body="*"

NOT orig_mime_type_first_stated IN (
    "application/x-www-form-urlencoded",
    "application/ocsp-request"
)

NOT user_agent IN (
    "MicroMessenger Client",
    "Dalvik*",
    "AliPayWallet*"
)

| eval dest_port=coalesce(dest_port, 'id.resp_p'),

rules.title: Certificate expiring after 2030 still uses classical signature
rules.desc: A TLS or Key Vault certificate has an expiry date after 2030-01-01 and is signed with a quantum-vulnerable classical algorithm. Long-lived certificates are the primary harvest-now- decrypt-later risk vector. Reissue with a PQ-hybrid signature or shorten validity window.
rules.query:
PQReadiness_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where AssetKind in ("tls-cert", "kv-cert")
| where QuantumPosture == "vulnerable"
| where isnotnull(ExpiresOn) and ExpiresOn > datetime(2030-01-01)
| project TimeGenerated, ResourceId, ResourceName, AssetIdentifier, SignatureAlgorithm, ExpiresOn, RiskScore, SubscriptionId, ResourceGroup
| order by ExpiresOn desc

rules.title: New quantum-vulnerable resource appeared
rules.desc: A resource with quantum-vulnerable posture appeared that was not observed in the previous 24-hour scan cycle. Investigate whether this is a new deployment that should have been provisioned with PQ-hybrid cryptography from the start.
rules.query:
let previous = PQReadiness_CL
  | where TimeGenerated between (ago(2d) .. ago(1d))
  | where QuantumPosture == "vulnerable"
  | distinct AssetIdentifier;
PQReadiness_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where QuantumPosture == "vulnerable"
| where AssetIdentifier !in (previous)
| project TimeGenerated, ResourceId, ResourceName, AssetIdentifier, AssetKind, Algorithm, PostureReason, RiskScore, SubscriptionId, ResourceGroup

rules.title: Quantum-vulnerable certificate on Entra app registration
rules.desc: An Entra ID (Azure AD) app registration or service principal has a certificate credential using a classical algorithm (RSA or elliptic-curve) that is vulnerable to Shor's algorithm. These certificates authenticate workloads and service-to-service flows -- a compromised cert allows impersonation of the application identity. Rotate to a PQ-hybrid certificate or shorten the validity window.
rules.query:
PQReadiness_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where AssetKind in ("entra-app-cert", "entra-sp-credential")
| where QuantumPosture == "vulnerable"
| extend AppId = extract(@'"appId":"([^"]+)"', 1, Metadata)
| project TimeGenerated, ResourceName, AssetIdentifier, Algorithm, KeySize, PostureReason, RiskScore, ExpiresOn, AppId
| order by RiskScore desc

rules.title: Quantum-vulnerable key detected in Key Vault
rules.desc: A key in Azure Key Vault has been classified as quantum-vulnerable (RSA or elliptic-curve). These key types are broken by Shor's algorithm on a sufficiently large fault-tolerant quantum computer. Rotate to a PQ-hybrid key (ML-KEM, ML-DSA) or plan migration before the harvest-now-decrypt-later window closes for long-lived data.
rules.query:
PQReadiness_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where AssetKind == "kv-key"
| where QuantumPosture == "vulnerable"
| extend AlgorithmDetail = strcat(Algorithm, iif(isnotnull(KeySize), strcat("-", tostring(KeySize)), ""))
| project TimeGenerated, ResourceId, ResourceName, AssetIdentifier, AlgorithmDetail, PostureReason, RiskScore, SubscriptionId, ResourceGroup
| order by RiskScore desc

rules.title: Public TLS certificate with classical signature on Application Gateway
rules.desc: An Application Gateway or Front Door is presenting a TLS certificate signed with a classical algorithm (RSA / ECDSA) that is quantum-vulnerable. If the certificate's validity extends past the plausible arrival of cryptographically-relevant quantum computers, replace with a PQ-hybrid certificate now.
rules.query:
PQReadiness_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where AssetKind == "tls-cert"
| where QuantumPosture == "vulnerable"
| project TimeGenerated, ResourceId, ResourceName, AssetIdentifier, SignatureAlgorithm, ExpiresOn, RiskScore, SubscriptionId, ResourceGroup
| order by RiskScore desc

rules.title: Appliance certificate expiring within 30 days with classical algorithm
rules.desc: A network appliance TLS certificate is expiring within the next 30 days and uses a classical (quantum-vulnerable) signature algorithm. Certificate renewal is an ideal time to migrate to a PQ-hybrid certificate. If the certificate is renewed with a classical algorithm, the harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure window resets for the new validity period.
rules.query:
PQReadiness_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where AssetKind == "tls-cert"
| where QuantumPosture == "vulnerable"
| where isnotnull(ExpiresOn) and ExpiresOn between (now() .. ago(-30d))
| where ResourceType has_any ("F5", "CheckPoint", "PaloAlto", "Cisco", "Fortinet")
    or Metadata contains "certificate_expiring"
| project TimeGenerated, ResourceName, ResourceType, AssetIdentifier, SignatureAlgorithm, ExpiresOn, RiskScore, PostureReason, SubscriptionId, ResourceGroup
| order by ExpiresOn asc

rules.title: PQC-ready appliance detected -- quantum-safe posture confirmed
rules.desc: A network appliance has been confirmed as post-quantum ready. This may indicate a QCrypton PQC Engine deployment on F5 BIG-IP, a hybrid key exchange (X25519MLKEM768) negotiation, or an ML-DSA/ML-KEM certificate in use. This is a positive signal -- the appliance is protected against harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks.
rules.query:
PQReadiness_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where QuantumPosture == "compliant"
| where Metadata contains "pqc_hybrid_key_exchange"
    or Metadata contains "f5_pqc_engine_active"
    or Metadata contains "f5_cert_pqc_ready"
    or Metadata contains "pqc_cert_ready"
| project TimeGenerated, ResourceName, ResourceType, AssetIdentifier, Algorithm, PostureReason, SubscriptionId, ResourceGroup

rules.title: Network appliance serving quantum-vulnerable certificate
rules.desc: A network appliance (F5 BIG-IP, Check Point, Palo Alto, Cisco ASA, or Fortinet) is presenting a TLS certificate signed with a classical algorithm (RSA/ECDSA) that is vulnerable to quantum attack. These appliances terminate TLS for critical internal traffic and are prime harvest-now-decrypt-later targets. Migrate to PQ-hybrid certificates or deploy QCrypton PQC Engine to front the appliance.
rules.query:
PQReadiness_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where AssetKind == "tls-cert"
| where QuantumPosture == "vulnerable"
| where ResourceType has_any ("F5", "CheckPoint", "PaloAlto", "Cisco", "Fortinet")
| project TimeGenerated, ResourceName, ResourceType, AssetIdentifier, Algorithm, SignatureAlgorithm, KeySize, ExpiresOn, RiskScore, PostureReason, SubscriptionId, ResourceGroup
| order by RiskScore desc

rules.title: High-risk internal endpoint with critical quantum vulnerability
rules.desc: An internal endpoint or network appliance has a risk score above 20, indicating critical or high severity quantum vulnerabilities. This may include expired certificates on appliances, RSA keys shorter than 2048 bits, or multiple compounding vulnerabilities on the same endpoint. Immediate remediation is recommended.
rules.query:

| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where QuantumPosture == "vulnerable"

rules.title: Internal endpoint using TLS protocol below 1.3

| where QuantumPosture in ("vulnerable", "partial")
| where Metadata contains "TLSv1.0" or Metadata contains "TLSv1.1" or Metadata contains "TLSv1.2"
| project TimeGenerated, ResourceName, ResourceType, AssetIdentifier, PostureReason, RiskScore, SubscriptionId, ResourceGroup

rules.desc: Detects suspicious commands as identified in CISA Living off the Land pdf. Alone they may be normal but in concert, they may be worth looking into
rules.author: Google Cloud Security
rules.query:
/*

rule recon_suspicious_commands_cisa_report {

  meta:
    author = "Google Cloud Security"
    description = "Detects suspicious commands as identified in CISA Living off the Land pdf. Alone they may be normal but in concert, they may be worth looking into"
    rule_id = "mr_66edb4f7-a7e2-4ce6-a247-d09319b7eeea"
    rule_name = "Recon Suspicious Commands CISA Report"
    type = "hunt"
    platform = "Windows"
    data_source = "microsoft sysmon, microsoft windows events"
    reference = "https://media.defense.gov/2023/May/24/2003229517/-1/-1/0/CSA_Living_off_the_Land.PDF"
    severity = "Low"
    priority = "Low"

  events:
    $process.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_LAUNCH"
    $process.principal.hostname = $hostname
    $process.target.process.command_line = $command_line

    // cisa report referenced cmd /c in their report throughout, can filter this in/out for tuning as needed
    // other wmic switches like /user and /password, these have been excluded to focus on the commands being issued since local access does not require these
    (
        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `(^|[\\/])7z\b.*?\ba\b.*?\b-p.*?\bc:\\windows\\temp\\.*\.7z`) nocase or
        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `(^|[\\/])pcwrun\.exe\b.*?\bc:\\Users\\Administrator\\Desktop\\Win\.exe`) nocase or
        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `(^|[\\/])(cmd(\.exe)?|cmdbak)\b.*?[/c]\b.*?\bping\b.*?\b-n\b.*?\b1\b.*?\b127\.0\.0\.1\b.*?\bc:\\Windows\\temp\\(putty|tmp)\.log`) nocase or
        // The following line could be swapped for the previous line for a looser match. It was observed during testing that a c2 running powershell logged putty.log as a file creation but not in the command line process event
        //re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `(^|[\\/])ping\b.*?\b-n\b.*?\b1\b.*?\b127\.0\.0\.1`) nocase or
        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `(^|[\\/])(cmd(\.exe)?|cmdbak)\b.*?[/c]\b.*?\bdir\b.*?\b127\.0\.0\.1\\c\$.*?/od`) nocase or
        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `(^|[\\/])ping\b.*?\b-a\b.*?\b-n\b.*?\b1\b`) nocase or
        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `(^|[\\/])wmic\b.*?\bprocess\b.*?\bcall\b.*?\bcreate\b.*?\bnet\b.*?\bstop\b.*?\bC:\\Windows\\Temp\\tmp\.log"`) nocase or
        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `\\ADMIN\$\\__.*2>&1`) nocase or
        //The following line could be swapped for the previous line for a looser match, but potentially noisier
        //re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `\\ADMIN\$\\__`) nocase or
        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `(^|[\\/])net\b.*?\buse\b.*?\b127\.0\.0\.1\\ipc\$.*?/y.*?/d`) nocase or
        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `(^|[\\/])powershell\b.*?\bstart-process\b.*?\b-filepath\b.*?\bc:\\windows\\temp\\.*\.bat\b.*?\b-windowstyle\b.*?\bHidden`) nocase or
        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `(^|[\\/])rar\.exe\b.*?\ba\b.*?\bc:\\Windows\\temp\\.*?D:\\`) nocase or
        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `(^|[\\/])wmic\b.*?\b(cmd(\.exe)?|cmdbak)\b.*?[/c]\b.*?\bwhoami`) nocase or
        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `(^|[\\/])xcopy\b.*?\bc:\\windows\\temp\\hp\b.*?\bd:\\`) nocase
    )

  match:
    $hostname over 15m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = 35
    $event_count = count_distinct($process.metadata.id)
    $unique_command_line_threshold = 5
    // added to populate alert graph with additional context
    // Commented out principal.hostname because it is already represented in graph as match variable. If match changes, can uncomment to add to results
    //$principal_hostname = array_distinct($process.principal.hostname)
    $principal_process_pid = array_distinct($process.principal.process.pid)
    $principal_process_command_line = array_distinct($process.principal.process.command_line)
…(truncated, open the source for the full rule)

rules.title: Java Base64 Decoder Argument Exceptions
rules.desc: The analytic finds Java Base64 decoder references and argument exceptions on the same JVM process within one minute. JIT messages add context when present. These logs indicate decoder activity and errors, but do not prove that a native overwrite or code execution occurred.
rules.logsource: Java HotSpot Exceptions, Java HotSpot JIT
rules.author: Onur Mustafa Erdogan, Nasreddine Bencherchali, Splunk
fp: Applications that routinely decode malformed Base64 can produce these events. The decoder and exception may come from separate requests within the same minute; review the surrounding application and network events.
rules.how: Configure java_hotspot_exceptions and java_hotspot_jit for the indexes and sourcetypes in your environment. A stock HotSpot JVM does not create exception or JIT log files; its default unified logging sends warning and error messages to stdout. Tomcat JULI logs under CATALINA_BASE/logs, Spring Boot'…
rules.query:
(`java_hotspot_jit` OR `java_hotspot_exceptions`)
(
    "*Input byte array has wrong*"
    OR "*IllegalArgumentException*"
    OR "*Base64$Decoder*"
    OR "*java/util/Base64*"
    OR "*OSR invalidation of lower level*"
)

| rex field=_raw "^\[(?<jvm_event_time_raw>[^\]]+)\]\[(?<jvm_pid_raw>\d+)\]\[(?<jvm_level_raw>[^\]]+)\]\[(?<jvm_tags_raw>[^\]]+)\]\s*(?<jvm_message_raw>.*)"

| eval process_id=coalesce(jvm_pid_raw,jvm_pid,process_id),
    jvm_message=coalesce(jvm_message_raw,jvm_message),
    event_time=_time

| where isnotnull(process_id)

| rex mode=sed field=jvm_message "s/0x[0-9A-Fa-f]{8,16}/0xXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX/g"
| rex mode=sed field=jvm_message "s/\s+bci\s+\d+\s+/ bci XXX /g"
| rex mode=sed field=jvm_message "s/^\d+\s+/XXXX /g"

| eval has_argument=if(match(jvm_message,"(?i)Input byte array has wrong|IllegalArgumentException"),1,0),
    has_decoder=if(match(jvm_message,"Base64[$]Decoder|java/util/Base64|Input byte array has wrong 4-byte ending unit"),1,0)

| eval reason=case(
    match(jvm_message,"(?i)Input byte array has wrong"),"Tailing byte exception",
    match(jvm_message,"(?i)OSR invalidation of lower level"),"JIT activity",
    has_decoder==1,"Base64 decoder reference",
    has_argument==1,"Argument exception"
)

| bin _time span=1m

| stats count
        min(event_time) AS firstTime
        max(event_time) AS lastTime
        max(has_argument) AS has_argument
        max(has_decoder) AS has_decoder
        values(sourcetype) AS sourcetype
        dc(sourcetype) AS dc_sourcetype
        values(source) AS source
        dc(source) AS dc_source
        values(reason) AS reason
        values(jvm_message) AS jvm_message
        BY _time host process_id

| where has_argument==1 AND has_decoder==1

| rename host AS dest

| fields - has_argument has_decoder

| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| `java_base64_decoder_argument_exceptions_filter`

  ),

  file_path=if(EventID==11,TargetFilename,null()),
  file_name=if(EventID==11,mvindex(split(TargetFilename,"/"),-1),null())

| bin _time span=1m

| stats count

        max(event_time) AS lastTime
        max(has_argument) AS has_argument
        max(has_decoder) AS has_decoder
        max(has_activity) AS has_activity
        values(sourcetype) AS sourcetype
        dc(sourcetype) AS dc_sourcetype
        values(activity) AS activity
        values(jvm_message) AS jvm_message
        values(process_name) AS process_name
        values(process) AS process
        values(file_name) AS file_name
        values(file_path) AS file_path
        BY _time observed_host process_id

| where has_argument==1 AND has_decoder==1 AND has_activity==1

| rename observed_host AS dest

| eval reason="Java Base64 exception observed with ".mvjoin(activity," and ")

| fields - has_argument has_decoder has_activity activity

| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| `java_base64_exception_with_process_or_file_activity_filter`

let failed_signins = table(tableName)
| where ResultType == "50057"
| where ResultDescription in ("User account is disabled. The account has been disabled by an administrator.", "The user account is disabled.");
let disabled_users = failed_signins | summarize by UserPrincipalName;
table(tableName)
  | where ResultType == 0
  | where isnotempty(UserPrincipalName)
  | where UserPrincipalName !in (disabled_users)
| summarize
        successfulAccountsTargettedCount = dcount(UserPrincipalName),

        successfulApplicationSet = make_set(AppDisplayName, 100)
    by IPAddress, Type
    // Assume IPs associated with sign-ins from 100+ distinct user accounts are safe

  | join kind=inner (failed_signins
| summarize
    StartTime = min(TimeGenerated),
    EndTime = max(TimeGenerated),
    totalDisabledAccountLoginAttempts = count(),

    applicationsTargeted = dcount(AppDisplayName),
    disabledAccountSet = make_set(UserPrincipalName, 100),
    disabledApplicationSet = make_set(AppDisplayName, 100)
by IPAddress, Type
| order by totalDisabledAccountLoginAttempts desc) on IPAddress
| project StartTime, EndTime, IPAddress, totalDisabledAccountLoginAttempts, disabledAccountsTargettedCount, disabledAccountSet, disabledApplicationSet, successfulApplicationSet, successfulAccountsTargettedCount, successfulAccountSigninSet, Type
| order by totalDisabledAccountLoginAttempts};
let aadSignin = aadFunc("SigninLogs");
let aadNonInt = aadFunc("AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs");
union isfuzzy=true aadSignin, aadNonInt
| join kind=leftouter (
    BehaviorAnalytics
    | where ActivityType in ("FailedLogOn", "LogOn")
